name: showreel-style-c-details

voice.text: Why do good apps feel so smooth? One: the copy button springs into Copied, and lands in half a second. Two: the switch knob stretches as it slides, then settles round again. Three: the toast eases up from below, then swipes away with a flick. Save all three for your next app.

caption: Why do good apps feel so smooth? Three small motions, slowed down so you can see them. 1) A copy button that springs into Copied: transition on width with linear(), 500 ms, one overshoot. 2) A switch knob that stretches as it slides: cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1) plus a squash keyframe on scale. 3) A toast that eases up and settles: @starting-style gives it a place to start from, no JavaScript. linear() works in Chrome 113, Firefox 112 and Safari 17.2; @starting-style in Chrome 117, Firefox 129 and Safari 17.5. Save it for your next app, or send it to a designer friend.

MDN, the scale and translate properties; BCD: Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1

tip.title: Three small motions that make an app feel smooth
tip.why: A UI change that springs, stretches or settles reads as a response to your finger; one that jumps reads as a glitch. Each of these is one transition line.
